content:
maya: heads-up — found a recurring gap in how exemplars are being propagated from metrics -> traces. this is causing mismatches in cost-attribution dashboards and the 'top callers by token' card is noisy.

alex: can you sketch the repro? is this OTLP -> prometheus -> remote-write flow or something earlier?

maya: OTLP export from services -> metrics ingest. services attach exemplars via the OTLP metric Exemplars API with trace_id. but our ingest path strips out the resource.billing.key when rewriting labels, so exemplars sometimes lose tenant context.

sam: ah right — we canonicalize labels for cardinality reasons and that transform runs before exemplar attachment. so exemplars end up with the service-level labels but without the billing tag.

jess: that explains why the cost attribution join fails for exemplars. the UI expects exemplar.trace_id + billing.key to join into traces/cost. without billing.key we either drop or misattribute.

liam: quick brainstorm: we can (A) change transform ordering so resource labels are materialized before exemplar attach, (B) carry a separate exemplar_envelope with original resource payload, or (C) attach a lightweight reference id and resolve billing.key in a later join. each has tradeoffs.

alex: tradeoffs: (A) simpler but increases cardinality earlier in pipeline — risks ingestion QPS spikes. (B) keeps original context but doubles envelopes and storage overhead. (C) keeps low cardinality but requires a low-latency lookup service for every exemplar reference — operational complexity and latency added to queries.

maya: also note exemplars are rare-ish, but certain endpoints (batch ingesters) emit a lot. we saw a single service emit 20k exemplars/min which blew up the exemplar retention storage in the canary zone.

sam: proposal: introduce exemplar sampling policy + preservation rules. i.e. keep exemplars for: errors, latency > p99, and top-N by token count per minute. everything else sampled at 1%. plus preserve billing.key by carrying a tiny shadow label that is prunable (e.g., _bk_ref) which points to a compact lookup table keyed by {service, host, minute}.

jess: i like the top-N idea. for cost dashboards we only need exemplars for the heavy hitters. can we compute top-N in the ingest stream and tag exemplars with a boolean keep_exemplar?

liam: yes — we already do rolling top-k for trace sampling. we can reuse that operator. operator would mark exemplar.keep=true and enrich with billing.key before downstream label-slimming. others get sampled and lose exemplar details.

alex: implementation notes: the operator needs access to billing.key mapping (resource attrs) and token_count metric. order: 1) receive metric with exemplar + resource attrs 2) compute token_count aggregation per (service, route) window 3) decide keep_exemplar for incoming exemplar 4) if keep, materialize billing.key label and forward exemplar payload 5) if not keep, either drop exemplar or forward exemplar with minimal ref.

maya: what about queries that try to link exemplar -> trace later? we need the trace_id preserved always. even samples must have trace_id so debugging still works even if we don't keep billing.key.

sam: agreed. always preserve trace_id in exemplar envelope, but only keep the full label set when keep_exemplar=true. this reduces cardinality impact while preserving linkability.

jess: storage/warehouse impact: we'll need a slightly different schema for exemplars in long-term storage: exemplar_record {ts, metric_name, trace_id, exemplar_labels, billing_key (nullable), token_count, keep_flag}. billing_key nullable for sampled ones. should be compacted weekly.

liam: rollout plan: feature gate behind org-level flag. initially enable in dev and one canary prod region for 10% of services. add metric: exemplar_ownership_mismatch_count and exemplar_billing_missing_count. monitor for spikes.

alex: edge cases: 1) OTLP exporters that embed billing.key only as resource attribute, not label — ensure mapping works. 2) metrics that attach exemplars after scrubbing — we should document that exemplars must be emitted with trace_id at the point of capture.

maya: question for ops: does the downstream trace store accept trace_id-only joins? if not, we'll need a small join index.

observability-bot: new ticket created: O11-452 "exemplar propagation: preserve billing key + sampling policy" assigned to @liam, priority P2. link: https://issues.redwood.example/O11-452

jess: security note: billing_key is sensitive and must be redacted in public logs. in internal paths it's fine, but don't echo into user-facing endpoints. add KMS audit for exemplar enrichment operator.

sam: perf numbers we need before changing order: measure delta on cardinality when materializing billing_key early for a 24h window on canary. if delta < 2x it's probably acceptable.

maya: next actions: liam to prototype operator + small canary, sam to run cardinality delta test with current telemetry snapshot, alex/jess to update data model and UI join logic to handle nullable billing_key. plan check-in end of week.

liam: ack, will prototype.

maya: thanks all — this should reduce the noisy misattributions once we have the keep_exemplar path working. :thumbsup:

alex: one more thought — add a flag to the remote-write export to optionally drop exemplars entirely for downstream cheaper regions (dedicated customers might want to keep everything). admin config per-customer.

jess: yep make it configurable per-tenant. we'll need CSP/contract language for Dedicated/private tenants re: exemplar retention.

maya: cool. I'll sync with product on the contract language. meeting adjourned.
